reviewed_by: Claude Sonnet blind reviewer, batch C11 (re-review after boilerplate rejection), 2026-08-12

samples_reviewed.question_text: Two lines that cross at exactly one point are called ___.
Two intersecting lines that do NOT form a right angle are called ___.
The corner of a square shows which type of lines meeting?
The edges of a ruler's two long sides are an example of what type of lines?
Two lines that cross at exactly one point are called ___.
The corner of a square shows which type of lines meeting?
The edges of a ruler's two long sides are an example of what type of lines?
Train tracks that run side by side without meeting are an example of ___.
A street crossing where roads meet at right angles shows which line relationship?
Two lines that never meet, no matter how far they extend, are called ___.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency text 'Recognize and draw parallel, intersecting, and perpendicular lines.' names two verbs, but all 10 samples are fill-in-the-blank multiple-choice items that ask the student to name a relationship already shown (e.g. 'The corner of a square shows which type of lines meeting?'); the 'draw' verb is addressed in 0 of the 10 samples.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Of the competency's two named sub-cases, 'recognize' is exercised in all 10 samples but 'draw' is exercised in none: no sample instructs the student to construct, sketch, or mark a pair of parallel, intersecting, or perpendicular lines, so a named sub-case is entirely absent from the packet.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Every sample is a single-sentence stem with one blank and four short options, using concrete Grade 3 referents such as 'The edges of a ruler's two long sides' and 'Train tracks that run side by side without meeting are an example of ___.' with no multi-step reasoning or symbolic notation beyond the three target terms.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Contextual variety exists across the 10 samples (definitional stems like 'Two lines that never meet, no matter how far they extend' alongside real-world referents like 'A street crossing where roads meet at right angles'), but every sample shares the identical mcq fill-in-the-blank shape, so no sample varies the task type toward the production side of the competency.

competency_alignment.rationale: Across all 10 samples the varying element is the illustrative context or definitional phrasing (ruler edges, train tracks, a square's corner, a street crossing), not an unrelated axis such as numeric magnitude, so every sample keeps difficulty tied to line-relationship identification rather than drifting into a different skill.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: This geometry node has no numeric ceiling to check; the referenced objects (a ruler's edges, train tracks, a square's corner, a street crossing) are everyday concrete items with no coordinate grids, angle measurements, or multi-shape figures that would exceed Grade 3 Quarter 1 scope.
